basic_info.name: ABDM HealthDocumentRecord profile (NRCeS FHIR Implementation Guide for ABDM)
basic_info.description: HealthDocumentRecord is one of the seven Composition-based 'Clinical Artifact' profiles in the NRCeS FHIR Implementation Guide for ABDM, the national interoperability standard published by the National Resource Centre for EHR Standards (NRCeS, C-DAC Pune) under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare for the National Health Authority's Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission. Its own definition states that it 'represents the unstructured historical health records as a single or multiple Health Record Documents generally uploaded by the patients through the Health Locker' - i.e., it is the profile explicitly named for patient-uploaded scans and legacy paper. The single most load-bearing fact is that, unlike the sibling structured records (OPConsultRecord, PrescriptionRecord, DischargeSummaryRecord, DiagnosticReportRecord), HealthDocumentRecord's mandatory section entry is bound exclusively to DocumentReference, so it carries the raw digitized document (the scan itself, with inline base64 attachment data blessed as MUST-SUPPORT) but it has no medication, lab, diagnosis, allergy or vitals sections and no slot for a structured history extract. In other words, the profile is the sanctioned contract for the kiosk's scanned paper, but it is structurally incapable of carrying MediKiosk Module C's structured, physician-ready summary; that content must ride as separate resources under a structured artifact. It is a Composition profile: type is fixed to SNOMED CT 419891008 ('Record artifact') with display 'Record artifact', section.code is fixed to the same code, mandatory elements are status, type, subject (Reference Patient), date, author (1..*) and title, attester is Must Support (mode 1..1, required binding personal|professional|legal|official - the contract-level slot for the physician verify/attest step), encounter is optional 0..1, custodian is optional 0..1, and section.entry is 1..* Reference(DocumentReference). It is emitted inside a DocumentBundle (Bundle.type = document), FHIR R4 (4.0.1) only. The currently published version is v6.5.0 (generated 2025-05-08); a v7.0.0 preview build (generated 2026-07-15) keeps the profile essentially unchanged.
basic_info.organization: National Resource Centre for EHR Standards (NRCeS), a programme by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), Government of India, hosted at C-DAC Pune; published for the National Health Authority (NHA) and the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM). The ABDM clinical artifacts, including HealthDocumentRecord, are authored and versioned by NRCeS.
basic_info.country: India (national standard for the ABDM ecosystem; authored in Hindi/English India governance context).
basic_info.status: Production / published national standard. Version 6.5.0 is the current published release of the FHIR Implementation Guide for ABDM (released 2025-05-08, marked 'active'). A v7.0.0 preview/development build (draft as of 2026-07-15) is available on NRCeS's preview site and continues to define HealthDocumentRecord; the v7.0.0 build is explicitly labelled a 'Local Development build' and is not yet the ratified published release. The profile's formal page carries a 'Draft as of 2020-08-17' status banner (a stale page-level date reused across the IG) despite the IG itself being in active release.

technical_features.what_it_does: HealthDocumentRecord defines the minimum-conformance Composition structure for exchanging unstructured historical health records (scanned paper: old prescriptions, discharge summaries, lab reports, diagnostic images and similar documents) that patients upload to or carry into the ABDM ecosystem. Functionally it is a thin, code-fixed wrapper: it says 'this bundle is a record artifact', points at a patient, dates and attributes the record, and nests one mandatory section whose entries are references to DocumentReference resources that hold the actual scanned content. It is therefore a transport-and-attestation envelope for documents, not a structured history model. For summary generation it is relevant as the profile that legitimises the digitized-paper half of the pipeline and, critically, as the profile that cannot itself hold a structured summary - pushing the structured output decision toward OPConsultRecord (physician consult) or, in the v7.0.0 preview, the new Indian Patient Summary (INPS).
technical_features.architecture: A FHIR R4 (4.0.1) StructureDefinition derived from the base Composition resource, published as a NRCeS ABDM profile. Composition.type.coding is fixed (system http://snomed.info/sct, code 419891008, display 'Record artifact'); Composition.section.code.coding is fixed to the same SNOMED 419891008/'Record artifact'. Mandatory (1..1) elements: status (required binding CompositionStatus: preliminary|final|amended|entered-in-error), type, subject (Reference Patient, reference 1..1), date (dateTime), title (string), and section (BackboneElement). Author is 1..* (Reference Practitioner|Organization|PractitionerRole|Patient|Device|RelatedPerson). attester is 0..* Must Support with mode 1..1 (required binding personal|professional|legal|official) and optional party. encounter and custodian are 0..1. section.entry is 1..* Reference(DocumentReference) and section.author 0..*. It is designed to be the first entry of a Bundle of type document, conformant to the sibling DocumentBundle profile; the referenced DocumentReference profile (also NRCeS-published) carries the attachment, with inline base64 attachment.data as MUST-SUPPORT. The IG is delivered as standard FHIR R4 conformance artefacts (StructureDefinition JSON/XML/TTL plus examples) and is validated with ordinary FHIR R4 validators (e.g., HAPI FHIR).
technical_features.inputs: The profile consumes: patient identity (subject reference), an authoring practitioner/organization/device/patient reference, an editing date, a human title, and one or more referenced DocumentReference resources whose attachments are the digitized historical documents (scans/photos/PDFs, typically with base64 attachment.data). It does not consume structured clinical data - there are no slots for observations, medications, conditions or allergies.
technical_features.outputs: A FHIR R4 Bundle of type document (conformant to the DocumentBundle profile) whose first entry is a HealthDocumentRecord Composition, with status/type/subject/date/author/title plus one mandatory section referencing DocumentReference entries carrying the scanned documents. In ABDM exchange terms this becomes an HIE (health information exchange) payload shareable across the ecosystem, and can be pushed to/through the ABDM Health Locker and HIP/HIU flows. It does not output any structured, coded clinical summary.
technical_features.standards_compliance: Conformance is published and machine-validatable, not merely claimed: HealthDocumentRecord is a formal FHIR R4 StructureDefinition with differential/snapshot, fixed SNOMED CT codes, required/extensible bindings, and published example bundles. It conforms to FHIR R4 (4.0.1) and uses the base Composition and DocumentReference resources; terminology is SNOMED CT for the fixed type/section codes. It aligns with the ABDM Health Data Interchange Specifications 1.0, the EHR Standards for India (2016) and the National Digital Health Blueprint. Note it is a national (India-only) profile, not an HL7 International IPS profile; version 6.5.0 is the published contract, version 7.0.0 is preview. The companion DocumentBundle, DocumentReference, Patient, Practitioner and Organization profiles are all NRCeS-defined, so a bundle can be validated end-to-end against the same IG package (ndhm.in).
technical_features.offline_capability: The standard itself has no offline concept - it is a data-exchange contract, so offline behaviour is entirely the implementer's responsibility. For MediKiosk this matters: the kiosk can generate and store a HealthDocumentRecord-conformant Bundle locally (the JSON is self-contained, and DocumentReference MUST-SUPPORT inline base64 means the scan can travel inside the bundle without a separate binary fetch), then transmit it to a HIP/HIU/Health Locker endpoint when connectivity is available. No store-and-forward, encryption or sync mechanism is specified by the profile.
technical_features.languages_supported: The profile does not mandate a language. The base Composition.language element is present (preferred binding to CommonLanguages), so the document language can be declared (e.g., hi for Hindi), and free-text title/section text/narrative can be authored in Devanagari or English. There is no bilingual-document requirement, no translation profile, and no Indian-language value-set localisation in this profile itself. [uncertain]
technical_features.deployment_model: Not applicable as a deployment model - it is a standard, not software. It runs wherever a conformant FHIR R4 HIP/HIU/client executes. The ABDM ecosystem prescribes HIP (health information provider) and HIU (health information user) roles on top of the ABDM Sandbox (sandbox.abdm.gov.in); the kiosk would act as a HIP creating the record and the consultation/HIS side as HIU consuming it. No hardware requirement is stated.

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: Not applicable - this is a data-structure conformance profile, not a model or a system, so there are no accuracy, F1, ROUGE, BERTScore or error-rate figures. Its 'quality metric' is binary conformance: a bundle either validates against the HealthDocumentRecord StructureDefinition (and the fixed SNOMED type/section codes, mandatory elements and DocumentReference-only section entries) or it does not. Validation is performed with standard FHIR R4 validators against the ndhm.in package.
performance_metrics.latency: Not applicable. No latency, throughput or time-to-summary figures exist for a profile. The only performance-relevant property is structural weight: because HealthDocumentRecord embeds only references (and optionally inline base64 document data), its wire size is dominated by the scanned attachment, not by the Composition itself.
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: Not applicable as a runtime requirement. In practice, holding one HealthDocumentRecord bundle costs the memory/storage of its embedded DocumentReference attachment(s); inline base64 attachment.data inflates payload size by roughly a third versus raw bytes, which is a real consideration on a ~4GB kiosk if many high-resolution scans are bundled simultaneously.
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: Adoption is ecosystem-scale rather than product-scale: HealthDocumentRecord is one of the mandatory clinical-artifact profiles in the national ABDM FHIR IG used across India's ABDM HIUs/HIPs and the ABDM Health Locker, and NRCeS distributes the IG package (ndhm.in), usage samples (Java/.NET) and validation tooling. NRCeS publishes no per-profile instance counts. [uncertain]
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: Conformance is verified by validating instances against the published StructureDefinition using standard FHIR R4 validation (e.g., HAPI FHIR, which NRCeS points to and releases Java usage samples for; Matchbox-style validation is also possible). NRCeS publishes example bundles (e.g., Bundle-HealthDocumentRecord-example) as reference instances and provides an IG QA report. There is no clinical-quality or benchmark evaluation because the profile carries no clinical inference; it is a structural contract.

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: HealthDocumentRecord directly answers - and partly closes - the open question of which ABDM artifact should carry a kiosk-generated pre-visit summary. It is the named profile for the paper-scan half of MediKiosk: the digitized documents from Module B have a first-class, nationally sanctioned home as DocumentReference entries inside a HealthDocumentRecord Composition. But the profile is the evidence against using HealthDocumentRecord as the summary carrier: its section.entry is bound exclusively to DocumentReference and it defines no medication/lab/diagnosis/allergy/vitals sections, so Module C's structured, coded, physician-ready summary cannot live inside it. The right reading is a two-artifact emission: scans -> HealthDocumentRecord (raw documents), structured summary -> a structured artifact. The strongest update is the v7.0.0 preview, which adds the Indian Patient Summary (INPS) - an India-localised derivative of HL7 IPS with mandatory Problems/Allergies/Medication sections plus a Patient Story section and Plan of Care - giving Module C a plausible, standards-based destination for a patient-elicited structured summary that did not exist when the open question was first raised. The attester slot (Must Support, mode professional) also confirms at contract level that the physician verify/attest step Module C requires is native to the ABDM model.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt: (1) HealthDocumentRecord as the emission shape for the digitized-document half - raw scan as DocumentReference (inline base64 attachment.data is MUST-SUPPORT) inside a DocumentBundle, because it is the named national contract for patient-uploaded unstructured records; (2) the DocumentBundle + Composition-first-entry pattern and its mandatory status/type/subject/date/author/title skeleton as the reusable envelope for any Module C document; (3) the attester element with mode='professional' as the standards-native encoding of physician attestation; (4) validation against the published ndhm.in package via a standard FHIR R4 validator rather than a hand-rolled schema. Reject or adapt: (1) do NOT try to force the structured pre-visit summary into HealthDocumentRecord - it has no structured sections; (2) do NOT rely on the frozen v6.5.0 assumption that no summary profile exists - track the v7.0.0 INPS preview, since INPS is the emerging structured-summary home; (3) treat inline base64 attachments carefully on a ~4GB kiosk (size inflation and memory) and prefer referencing a Binary where a large scan is involved; (4) do not read the stale 'Draft as of 2020-08-17' banner as the profile's release date - the IG is in active release at v6.5.0.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: The core limitation is structural: HealthDocumentRecord is document-only and cannot carry structured clinical content, so it is not a summary profile despite superficially looking like a 'record'. Its section carries a single fixed SNOMED code ('Record artifact') for both the composition type and section code, so there is essentially one undifferentiated 'documents' section - no clinical categorisation. Version risk: the contract is moving (v6.5.0 published 2025-05-08; v7.0.0 preview built 2026-07-15 adds INPS and may renumber/re-shape things), and the profile page's own status date is misleading, so any emitter design must pin a version and re-check. Ecosystem risk: the profile assumes ABDM HIP/HIU and Health Locker plumbing; an offline-first kiosk must implement store-and-forward itself, and there is no residency/encryption guidance inside the profile. Terminology risk: fixed SNOMED CT codes require India SNOMED affiliate licensing awareness. Finally, because the summary-carrier question is only provisionally answered by a preview INPS, committing to an emitter today risks rework when v7.0.0 is ratified.
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: This is a national standard, not a competitor, so it neither strengthens nor erodes MediKiosk's differentiation by itself - but it constrains it. It supplies the mandatory, non-negotiable output contract for the scan half (raw documents -> DocumentReference inside HealthDocumentRecord/DocumentBundle), meaning ANY ABDM-conformant competitor must emit essentially the same document envelope; the defensible differentiation therefore cannot be 'we produce ABDM documents' but must sit above it. MediKiosk's stated differentiators - offline-first, India residency, NRCeS-conformant emission, per-field provenance and physician attestation - are all compatible with this profile: the attester slot even validates the attestation design. The one thing the profile plus the v7.0.0 INPS preview changes is that 'no NRCeS profile exists for patient-elicited summaries' is no longer fully true; the emerging INPS (with its Patient Story section) weakens a naive 'we invented the patient summary' claim, so MediKiosk's differentiation should rest on patient-elicited structured history generation, per-field provenance, and offline operation rather than on the existence of a summary format.

business_info.license: The NRCeS FHIR Implementation Guide for ABDM is published under a CC0 (Creative Commons public domain) notice on its pages (the IG footer carries the CC0 mark, consistent with HL7 FHIR IG licensing); there is no proprietary license on the profile definition itself. The ProfileDefinition and example artefacts are freely usable and redistributable. Note that terminology used by the profile (SNOMED CT) carries its own licensing frame (India SNOMED affiliate licence via NRCeS/MLDS), separate from the IG licence.
business_info.pricing: No cost. The ABDM FHIR profiles, IG, terminology packages and usage samples are government-published and free to download and implement.
business_info.funding: Government-funded: authored and maintained by NRCeS, a MoHFW programme at C-DAC Pune, for the National Health Authority's ABDM. Public-sector programme funding, not commercial.
business_info.commercial_status: A government programme standard, not a commercial product or service. Adoption is by regulation/ecosystem incentive rather than sale; there is no vendor, price or contract.

competition_ecosystem.competitors: Not a competitive product space, but adjacent artifact choices compete for the same slot: the sibling NRCeS profiles OPConsultRecord (structured consult note - the most likely carrier of Module C's physician-facing summary), PrescriptionRecord, DischargeSummaryRecord, DiagnosticReportRecord, WellnessRecord and ImmunizationRecord; the sibling DocumentBundle/DocumentReference profiles; and, from the v7.0.0 preview, the Indian Patient Summary (INPS), which is an India-localised derivative of HL7 International IPS and is the emerging structured-summary alternative. International prior art for the summary concept is HL7 IPS itself. Open-source competitor/alternative tooling around this contract includes HAPI FHIR, fhir.resources (Python) and matchbox.
competition_ecosystem.integrations: Integrations are the ABDM ecosystem: HIP (health information provider) and HIU (health information user) roles, the ABDM Health Locker (where patients upload/link documents), the ABDM Sandbox (sandbox.abdm.gov.in) for testing, and the wider HIE. On the tooling side, NRCeS publishes FHIR R4 usage samples in Java (HAPI HL7) and .NET (Firely), and the IG package ndhm.in is loadable in standard validators (HAPI FHIR, Matchbox). Terminology integrations tap NRCeS national releases: SNOMED CT India, CDCI (Common Drug Codes for India), CLCI (Common Lab Codes for India - LOINC subset), the India AYUSH Extension and the Bharat Health Terminology Service (BHTS).
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: The ABDM ecosystem is actively moving and Indian-specific terminology is maturing fast, which is a tailwind for MediKiosk: NRCeS re-launched a Bharat Health Terminology Service (BHTS, June 2026), published CLCI lab codes (June 2026), keeps releasing CDCI drug codes and the India AYUSH Extension, and expanded SNOMED's Global Patient Set (March 2026). Critically for Module C, the v7.0.0 preview folds in the Indian Patient Summary (INPS) built on HL7 IPS 2.0.0, signalling that ABDM is standardising a structured patient summary - this both validates a structured-summary goal and means any India emitter should watch v7.0.0. The ABDM model is consent-and-role based (HIP/HIU + Health Locker), and the DPDP Act 2023 / DPDP Rules 2025 timeline (phased, full compliance ~13 May 2027) sits over all of it. HealthDocumentRecord's fixed DocumentReference-only section is a hard reminder that the national contract deliberately separates 'documents' from 'structured clinical data'.

history.release_date: The HealthDocumentRecord profile page carries a 'Draft as of 2020-08-17' banner, reflecting its origin in the first NDHM/ABDM FHIR profiles published around August 2020 (the NRCeS news page records 'FHIR Profiles for NDHM Health Data Interchange' on 2020-08-28). The currently published IG release is v6.5.0, dated 2025-05-08. [uncertain] (the 2020-08-17 date is a reused page-level banner, not verified as the exact first publication of this specific profile).
history.key_milestones: 2020-08: first NDHM/ABDM FHIR profiles published (HealthDocumentRecord present from this era; profile banner 2020-08-17); NRCeS also released FHIR R4 usage samples in Java (Nov 2020). 2023: ABDM IG builds v2.5.0 -> v5.0.0 expand profiles (OPConsultRecord/immunization/NHCX/insurance) but HealthDocumentRecord's document-only design persists. 2024-01-24: v6.0.0 build (InvoiceRecord, urn:uuid references). 2025-05-08: v6.5.0 published (current active release; new/updated CodeSystems and ValueSets, profile updates). 2026-07-15: v7.0.0 preview build generated, adding the Indian Patient Summary (INPS) derived from HL7 IPS 2.0.0 via imposeProfile, while HealthDocumentRecord is retained essentially unchanged.
history.recent_changes_last_6_months: In the last six months the ABDM standard has been visibly active. The v7.0.0 preview (generated 2026-07-15, labelled a local development build) is the headline change: it introduces an 'INPS' (Indian Patient Summary) section with general guidance and a full artifacts list of ABDM+IPS dual-conformant profiles (INPS Bundle/Composition, Condition, AllergyIntolerance, MedicationStatement/Request, Immunization, Procedure, Observation variants, Patient Story, etc.), explicitly derived from HL7 International Patient Summary v2.0.0 and made dual-conformant to ABDM base profiles using the structuredefinition-imposeProfile extension. HealthDocumentRecord itself is unchanged between v6.5.0 and the v7.0.0 preview (same fixed SNOMED type/section codes, same DocumentReference-only section entry). On the terminology side within the window, NRCeS released CLCI lab codes and the India AYUSH Extension (2026-06-29), CDCI/DISB bundles (2026-08-31 and earlier), the India Patient Instructions Language Extension for SNOMED CT (2026-08-31) and launched the Bharat Health Terminology Service (2026-06-29). No change to the published v6.5.0 HealthDocumentRecord contract in this window; the mover is INPS in the v7.0.0 preview.

market_positioning.target_users: Health-IT implementers and vendors building ABDM-compliant software: HIPs that create/upload health records (hospitals, clinics, labs, PHR apps, kiosks) and HIUs that consume them, plus the ABDM Health Locker. Secondary users are the patients who upload historical records and the NHA/NRCeS as standard owners.
market_positioning.market_segment: National health-data interoperability / FHIR tooling - specifically the clinical-artifact profile set for ABDM health data interchange. It is not a summary-generation or clinical-intelligence product; it sits in the 'standards and outputs' layer that kiosk/intake products must emit against.
market_positioning.positioning_statement: In its own words, HealthDocumentRecord is defined as: 'The Clinical Artifact represents the unstructured historical health records as a single or multiple Health Record Documents generally uploaded by the patients through the Health Locker and can be shared across the health ecosystem,' and the IG positions itself as defining 'the minimum conformance requirements for accessing health data to achieve continuity of care in the Indian context' under ABDM Health Data Interchange Specifications 1.0.
